_note: The W9 execution-tier VERDICT corpus (/web/15 law 4: tiers are visible; rendering-1.0-finalization.md, the tier-equivalence lane). THE LAW: every action-tier body classifies ONCE, at parse/build time, into 'jse' (the portable subset — natively interpreted on iOS/Android, compiled closures on web) or 'js' (the escalation tier — a real sandboxed engine per /web/12), and the three classifiers — TS classifyBody (kernel/src/compile/tier.ts, the REFERENCE: a token screen over the reference tokenizer, and since the strict-rejection hardening also the compiler's subset gate), Kotlin TierClassifier.classify (Engine/Android core Tier.kt), Swift TierClassifier.classify (Engine/iOS/Tier.swift) — must never drift: a body that compiles on web but escalates natively (or vice versa) is exactly the silent divergence this corpus exists to catch. THE SCREEN: the beyond-subset keywords (class, extends, super, yield, with, debugger) escalate as real tokens; generator functions (`function *`) and labeled loops (`name: for|while|do`) escalate as shapes; the CONTEXTUAL rules keep lookalikes portable — get/set escalate only in the accessor shape (`get name (`), never as a call (`get('k')`) or a property read; member-position `with` after `.`/`?.` is the ARRAY METHOD (in the JSE method table, corpus stdlib-001 — LOAD-BEARING: the strict compiler throws JSESubsetError on a js verdict, so a false escalation here would reject a valid body); keywords inside string literals, template literals and comments are never tokens. Conservative in the safe direction: a missed construct classifies jse and runs exactly as today. CASE SHAPE: { name, body, tier: 'jse'|'js', reasonContains: <substring>|null } — reasonContains is stated for every js case and matched as a SUBSTRING of the runner's reason (wording may differ per runner — Kotlin/Swift say "'get' accessors are outside …" where TS says "'get' is outside …"; the substring is the stable part), and a jse verdict must carry NO reason (null on all three). An optional 'note' documents a surprising verdict. Every cross-runtime divergence bug becomes a case here in the same commit as its fix.

cases.name: for-of-loop
cases.body: for (const x of items) { total = total + x.price }

cases.name: store-counter-loop
cases.body: for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) { total = total + i }
cases.note: the PORTABLE counter idiom (store-var counter, no let) — the loop shape the monorepo working rules name as the portable spelling

cases.name: ternary-colon
cases.note: a ternary colon is not a label — only `name : (for|while|do)` escalates

cases.name: object-literal-keys
cases.note: object keys are not labels — `for:` here is a key, and no loop keyword follows the colon

cases.name: await-fetch
cases.note: await is in the JSE grammar; the `//` inside the URL string is protocol syntax, never a comment

cases.name: class-extends
cases.body: class Feed extends Base { render() { return 1 } }
cases.note: the screen walks left-to-right, so the reason names `class` (the first hit), not `extends` — the substring pins escalation without over-pinning which keyword is reported

cases.name: extends-as-object-key
cases.note: pins `extends` as a TOKEN cross-runtime: the screen is token-level, so a beyond-subset keyword escalates even in key position (unlike `for:`, which is not in the keyword set) — deliberate conservatism, identical on all three

cases.name: super-call
cases.note: bare `super(` — a DOTTED spelling like `super.init` lexes as one dotted ident on the TS reference tokenizer and would not pin the keyword; the call shape does, on all three

cases.name: yield-keyword
cases.note: yield inside a NON-star function pins the keyword itself; inside `function*` the generator rule fires first (see generator-function)

cases.name: object-getter-accessor
cases.note: the accessor shape `get name (` — the substring stops at the keyword because the wording differs per runner (TS: "'get' is outside …"; Kotlin/Swift: "'get' accessors are outside …")

cases.name: get-call
cases.note: a CALL named get — no identifier between `get` and `(`, so the accessor shape never forms

cases.name: array-with-member
cases.note: LOAD-BEARING: member-position `with` is the Array METHOD (JSE method table, corpus stdlib-001) — the strict compiler rejects on a js verdict, so a false escalation here breaks a valid body

cases.name: optional-chain-with-member
cases.note: `?.` is one op token on the TS reference tokenizer and lexes as `?` + `.` on the native word-lexers — the dot immediately before `with` exempts it either way

cases.name: unterminated-string
cases.note: ADJUSTED TO THE REFERENCE (2026-08-07): the fail-closed catch arm in tier.ts expects a tokenizer THROW, but the reference tokenizer deliberately RECOVERS from an unterminated literal (it consumes to EOF and emits the recovered string token — the lenient JSE tokenizer), and the native word-lexers recover the same way, so all three classify jse and the body runs identically everywhere (bug-for-bug portable, the JseRunner.kt NOTES discipline). The catch arm stays as defense-in-depth; if the reference tokenizer ever grows a throwing input, THAT input becomes the js-verdict case here in the same commit

cases.name: unterminated-block-comment
cases.note: same recovery law as unterminated-string: the comment strips to EOF on all three, so the keyword inside it never becomes a token
